title: You keep calling yourself who God already buried.
paragraphs: You keep calling yourself who God already buried.
But what if the version of you that you hate… is already dead?
And you’re still living like the grave has authority?
That quiet shame that follows you when no one’s watching.
That memory you wish you could delete.
That sin you swore you’d never go back to… but somehow did.
And now the voice in your head whispers:
So you smile in public… but inside, you feel disqualified.
Some of you aren’t struggling with sin anymore…
You’re struggling with the shame of who you used to be.
And that shame is louder than your faith.
It replays your worst moments like a courtroom.
It builds a case against you.
It reminds you of every failure, every secret, every compromise.
And it convinces you that THIS is your identity.
But Scripture interrupts that lie with a thunderclap.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
Some scholars interpret this as not just a personal change, but participation in God’s new creation reality—where the power of sin is broken and a new life has truly begun.
If you are in Christ, the person you keep accusing…
…no longer exists in the way you think.
Yes, there may still be consequences.
Because on the cross, Jesus didn’t negotiate with your sin.
“We know that our old self was crucified with Him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing…” — Romans 6:6
Your old self was not patched.
So why are you still introducing yourself as someone Jesus already put to death?
Why are you wearing chains that already broke?
Why are you bowing to a version of you that Christ nailed to the cross?
Because the Gospel is not behavior modification.
And now you live with Him.
“I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me…” — Galatians 2:20
That means your story didn’t end in failure.
And it restarted at an empty tomb.
Not between who you were and who you’re trying to be—
“The accuser of our brothers has been thrown down…” — Revelation 12:10
But it also points to the cross.
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” — Romans 8:1
So if you’re still living under it…
You’re believing something Jesus already broke.
Grace is not permission to stay the same.
Grace is the power to become who God already says you are.
That means repentance is not shame-driven.
You don’t repent to earn a new life.
You repent because you’ve been given one.
You don’t fight sin to be accepted.
You fight sin because you are accepted.
Because now you’re not crawling back to God hoping He’ll tolerate you.
You’re walking toward your Father who already chose you.
So what do you do with this?
You stop agreeing with your shame.
You stop rehearsing your past like it’s your identity.
You stop introducing yourself by your worst moment.
And you start aligning your mind with truth.
Even when your emotions lag behind.
Even when the old voice is loud.
“Be transformed by the renewal of your mind…” — Romans 12:2
Because transformation doesn’t happen when you feel new.
It happens when you believe what God said… until it reshapes how you live.
So let me ask you something direct.
Because one of them is lying.
And one of them bled for you.
You can keep carrying what Jesus already carried…
Or you can finally lay it down.
Agree with God about what is wrong.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
And then receive what you didn’t earn.
Because Jesus didn’t come to manage your shame.
Come out of agreement with the old you.
Come into the truth of who you are in Christ.
Save this so you can come back when the lies get loud.
From shame to freedom — because Jesus rewrites everything.
